slides.title: reduce
slides.sub: A two-argument function, a collection, an initial value
slides.main: The initial value guards against an empty collection; use built-ins for sums and maxima.

body.text:
from functools import reduce
import operator

print(reduce(operator.mul, [1, 2, 3, 4]))
print(reduce(lambda acc, s: acc + "-" + s, ["a", "b", "c"]))
print(reduce(operator.add, [], 0))
try:
    reduce(operator.add, [])
except TypeError as e:
    print(e)

slides.title: partial
slides.sub: Some arguments are already filled in
slides.main: Replaces a lambda that just plugs in ready values.

body.text:
from functools import partial

from_bin = partial(int, base=2)
print(from_bin("101"), from_bin("1111"))
power_of_2 = partial(pow, 2)
print(list(map(power_of_2, [1, 2, 3])))

slides.title: lru_cache
slides.sub: A repeated call with the same arguments comes from the cache
slides.main: Arguments must be hashable; the result must depend only on them.

body.text: Without a cache, fib(80) would take billions of years.

slides.title: operator: operators as functions
slides.main: Instead of a one-operator lambda, a ready and faster function.

body.text:
import operator
from functools import reduce

print(operator.add(2, 3), operator.mul(4, 5), operator.lt(1, 2))
print(list(map(operator.pow, [2, 3], [3, 2])))
print(reduce(operator.mul, range(1, 6)))

slides.title: itemgetter, attrgetter, methodcaller
slides.main: Several keys in itemgetter: sort by several fields in one line.

body.text:
from operator import itemgetter, attrgetter, methodcaller

users = [{"name": "Anna", "age": 31}, {"name": "Boris", "age": 25}]
print(sorted(users, key=itemgetter("age"))[0]["name"])
rows = [("b", 2), ("a", 2), ("c", 1)]
print(sorted(rows, key=itemgetter(1, 0)))

class P:
    def __init__(self, year):
        self.year = year

print([p.year for p in sorted([P(2000), P(1990)], key=attrgetter("year"))])
print(list(map(methodcaller("upper"), ["a", "b"])))

slides.title: cmp_to_key
slides.main: Need to sort someone else's way? The adapter turns a comparison into a key.

body.text: A comparison function returns a negative number, zero or a positive number.

slides.title: A pipeline without lambdas
slides.main: Use the tool that makes the text shorter without losing clarity.

body.text:
from operator import itemgetter

sales = [{"dept": "IT", "sum": 120}, {"dept": "HR", "sum": 70},
         {"dept": "IT", "sum": 30}, {"dept": "HR", "sum": 200}]
big = filter(lambda s: s["sum"] >= 50, sales)
ordered = sorted(big, key=itemgetter("dept", "sum"))
print([(s["dept"], s["sum"]) for s in ordered])

slides.title: Combining tools
slides.main: First check the standard library, then write your own.

body.text:
from functools import partial, reduce
import operator

print(list(map(partial(int, base=16), ["ff", "10", "a"])))
print(reduce(operator.or_, [1, 2, 4]))
print(list(map(operator.methodcaller("strip"), [" a ", "b "])))
